newsitem.title: USA: Tejas CEO comfortable with EPS estimates.
newsitem.headline: Tejas CEO comfortable with EPS estimates.

text.p: Tejas Gas Corp Chief Executive Officer Jay Precourt on Tuesday said he was comfortable with analysts' consensus estimates of $0.40 a share in the third quarter and $1.85 in the full year.
"We don't think they are off base," Precourt said of the First Call estimates. "It's that order of magnitude."
Precourt said the recent acquisition of the 2.3 billion cubic-feet-per-day Transok natural gas pipeline system in Oklahoma, Louisiana and Texas will add to earnings this year.
"Transok will be mildly accretive this year, significantly accretive next year and substantially accretive in the years after that," he told Reuters.

The Houston-based natural gas company has been slowly filling its natural gas storage facilities, which have a capacity of 155 billion cubic feet, ahead of the coming winter heating season. It has enough gas on hand now to meet contractual obligations, he said.

"We have filled up about half of our (100 billion cubic feet) working gas," he said. "(But) the economics have not justified or allowed owners of storage in producing areas to fill storage and protect themselves from price risk."
Relatively low storage levels nationwide are fueling expectations of wide price swings if severe winter weather sets in.

"There is a greater likelihood we'll get price spikes if we get cold weather this year than we have seen in the last four or five years," he said after a speech to Houston gas producers and royalty owners.
